finding.claim: Broken authorization: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so no authorization check is enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id (IDOR / missing access control). closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, showing the intended pattern.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry point; id attacker-controlled
account looked up by attacker-supplied id
canDelete(u, a) return value ignored; no exception thrown on denial

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) would enforce admin-or-owner but its result is unused; assertCanDelete (throws) is not used in this path; no other auth layer or annotation exists in the repo. Contrast with closeAccount line 29 which is guarded.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (lines 9-11) returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (throws) is used only in closeAccount at line 29. No other guards, annotations or callers exist in the repo.
verdict.reason: AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete() as a bare statement and ignores the boolean, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, whereas closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses the throwing assertCanDelete.
